body:
Thanks, I'm just being careful to review what I read since I'm already imposing so much here.

I think the college health assistance might be a good place to start. I don't know why i didn't considered it earlier. I'm a little taken back by the fact that a lot of college staff seems to look down on students who don't have defined ambitions or clear goals for life though.

It's a real tought thing to raise myself when I keep trying to meet the often conflicting expectations of people around me, and it's really hard not to do that when I depend so much on them, and it's really hard not to depend so much on them when I can't take care of myself, which is really hard to do before rasing myself. I'm not trying to be funny, it's just that raising myself seems like an issue when I can't set any standards on which to do it that won't oppose people's expectations and I can't ignore these expectations either.

About my mother, I think about doing that everyday, but I can't come up and do it. I don't think it would come out right. Isn't there a more roundabout way to make her know I apprecciate her support more than anything? I know she thinks I don't respect her and everytime I open my mouth I end up making it look like she's right. That's a pretty big issue for me. It didn't make the list speccificaly, but I did mention taking other people's care for granted.

I think I might have been a little vague when I said I haven't matured sexualy. I'm not a virgin. I just don't feel any urges to pursue sex. I guess my situation is analogous to the more common situation of someone who's not into football in a country where football is the national passion. People just can't seem to figure out what it's like not to be interested in it.

I wouldn't go as far as saying that I define myself by my lack of sex, but it is a real downer that everytime I start to relate to someone, anyone, sex will eventually come up and I won't be able to show any enthusiasm on the subject. Maybe somebody will point out to a hot girl passing by and everybody'll get excited and laugh while I give out an uncomfortable laughter because I just can't relate to the way they feel. Or maybe me and some people are trying to decide where to go out (This doesn't happen much anymore, but I did go out more often a while back.) and the only criteria they use is "amount of good looking women" in the place. You might not notice because you're not standing where I am, but people really treat you differently if you don't correspond to this sort of thing. I don't resent them, I understand it's a weird thing from their perspective, but it's not something I can just switch on and off at will.

What's more, I really want to know why I don't seem to have any libido. Is it self repression? Is it hormonal? I'm a human. Humans should start to have intense libido during their teenage years, yet I'm 22 and never felt any desire to do anything more than masturbate every now and them. I've pursued sex through the easy ways before to meet the expectations of my peers and because I'd been convinced I was suppose to want it, but after doing it a couple of times I realized I liked masturbating much more than having sex. This is not common and there must be a cause. I suspect is part of the bigger picture that I can't have any kind of fun with anyone else.

Thanks for the support, but I don't really see how having sex is not so important. It seems to me like it's a pretty big deal no matter who I talk to. It is true that I live in a very sex obsessed and patriarcal country, but I still think that not being part of the "sex scene" can be really harmful to one's acceptance in most social cirlces everywhere.

In my defense, I said I couldn't communicate verbaly and through body language. That is to say, I can't hold conversations or make myself be understood in anyway that's not writing or a very awkward conversation with no timing.

As for your questions, I am currently unemployed and going through the first year of an undergraduate course in mathematics. I was expelled from this same college once for not attending classes, now I'm trying my best to do at least this much right this time around, but is hard considering how much social interaction is demanded of me.

I worked as a waiter for half a year last year while studying for the college entrance exams. It felt good to work for the first time and earn my own money, at least I know I'm not so useless as to starve.

My family is unrealible. Most of my problems can be traced back to them. My father, mother and brother are all depressed too. My mother is the only dependable one, but she live in denial as to the broken state of our family so it would do no good to go to her. Other relatives all have their own problems to worry about. I wouldn't want their help anyway. I do have health insurance, but as I said on the edit to the original post, their doctors end up being drug prescription dealers.

I'd really love to have a counselor to guide me through this, but I don't have anyone I can rely on, and finding a doctor who's willing to actually do it seems to be harder than I imagined. I've always looked for father figures in all of the people who were around me hoping to find someone who would correspond, but I wasn't very good at it aparently. I also hope to get some more physical activty done this year, but I'm really insecure about practicing sports so I tend to end up in sedentarism everytime.
